subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a militarized cyberpunk truck model, roughly 7m long, with a simple skeleton setup using a root chassis joint plus wheel joints rather than a full character rig.

Working out proportions and layout...

Still placing windshield geometry...

Now I'm designing the armored cargo module with a chamfered extruded profile for the angular top ramps, finished in paneled iron, and adding a roof-mounted missile pod with tilted tube clusters at the rear.

For the pod, I'm merging the tube and casing geometries into a single mesh for efficiency, then placing it with rotation to achieve the upward tilt. Next I'm planning the roof turret assembly: a ring base, turret housing, twin barrel cannons, and a sensor eye, with yaw and pitch joints for articulation.

Now I'm positioning the missile pods on both sides of the container near the rear and the turret slightly forward of them, then moving to the front design with a wedge bumper, dozer plow, glowing cab headlights, grille, and an amber roof light bar. Finally I'm working out the six wheels with low-poly tires, radius and width specs, and glowing cyan hub rings with spokes.

I'm working out the three axle positions, adding wheel arches, fenders, and side armor skirts between the wheels, then moving underneath to the drive shaft and axle rods, and placing twin vertical exhaust stacks behind the cab with glowing amber tips.

Now I'm adding details: whip antennas with glowing red tips, a lathe-modeled satellite dish with cable sweeps, and thin cyan neon underglow strips along the chassis sides. For textures I'm planning SVG decals including "2077" text, a emblem, hazard stripes, headlight, windshield, side window, and rear camera screen graphics—aiming for roughly six textures and a moderate-length build.

I'm working out greebling for the container sides: scattering small randomized boxes with varying depths and sizes, merged by color into a few groups to keep geometry efficient. I'm also figuring out decal plane placement and orientation on the left/right container faces, making sure text and texture directions read correctly when viewed from outside given the plane's normal and up vectors.

Checking wheel positions against the chassis and container bounds, I realize the wheels would clip through the container at the rear axles, so I need to raise the container floor to clear the wheel tops, giving space for proper wheel arches around both front and rear wheels relative to the cab.

I'm shaping the container with a stepped profile from y 1.3 to 2.9, topping it with a turret extending to 3.6, giving a total height near 3.9 with the antenna included. I notice a gap forms between the container front (z=0.4) and the cab (starting z=0.9), so I'll need to fill that space to avoid an awkward gap.

Adjusting the cab's starting point to z=0.5 closes most of that gap. I'm placing exhaust stacks as cylinders near the cab's back face, positioned just outside the container edge so they sit adjacent rather than overlapping, extending taller than the cab roof up to around y=2.9-3.2, and now I'm working out the cab's height profile points.

Continuing the cab profile with a sloped hood section, then a windshield slope rising to the roof, checking the polygon order doesn't self-intersect. For the front face detail, I'm figuring out where to place a headlight/grille plane—calculating the exact z-depth where the sloped front surface sits at headlight height so the texture plane sits flush against it.

Adding a bumper box and a wedge-shaped plow at the front, tilted slightly, plus some cone spikes for detail. Then I'm working out side window placement on the cab, positioning them along the sloped roofline.

Shifting the window placement slightly to fix the sticking-out issue, then moving on to plan the turret: a joint-based assembly with a ring, chamfered body box, and twin barrels mounted on the chassis.

Barrels get muzzle brakes, and I'm adding a sensor sphere with a glowing red eye for detail. I'm working out joint orientation defaults—since parts use explicit "at" placement in model space, bone orientation mostly just affects posing, so I can keep things simple with the root chassis joint and default bone directions. Now defining the wheel joints as children of chassis, named by position (wheelFL, etc.) with their own roles.

Wheels probably don't need an explicit role, but I'll give the turret/gun hinge a "hinge" role since that's accepted. I'm being careful that parts without an explicit bone assignment could snap to the nearest joint instead of the chassis, so my part-builder helper defaults everything to bone: body to avoid that risk. For materials, I'm keeping the color count under 64 and designing an armor paint using large tarnished iron panels with rivet detailing, sizing texel density and paint resolution to match the model's total painted surface area.

For the cab, I'm writing a custom cyberpunk camo paint function that mixes a dark noisy base color, adds grime darkening near the bottom, and a cool highlight near the top using smoothstep blending based on surface normal and position, then layering panel lines on top with no rivets. I'm deciding glow effects should be reserved for headlights and light strips rather than textured surfaces like the windshield, since glow would wash out texture colors. Now I'm starting to define the texture set, beginning with the headlight texture.

I'm sketching out the rest of the textures: a glowing headlight panel with a dark grille and cyan-magenta lights, a windshield gradient with reflection streaks and HUD text that stays unglowed, a side emblem panel with hazard stripes and "ARES-77" lettering, a repeating hazard stripe pattern, a rear radar display that glows, and a neon sign using "NEXUS" instead of kanji since custom fonts may not render. I'm also considering a glowing hub ring texture for the wheels, skipping the dial texture for now.

Then I'm moving on to the actual model details: a rear face plane with glowing red tail lights and the radar screen, rear door lines, a roof lightbar on the cab with amber glow segments, vent grids and antenna whips on the container roof, and a tilted satellite dish built from a lathe geometry with a thin shell profile and support arm, positioned on the container's rear roof corner. I'm also weighing whether to add side fuel or ammo tanks between the axles, but considering skipping that for now.

I'm planning armor plates with hazard decals along the sides, and for the wheel hub bolts I want to avoid creating 36 separate small boxes, so I'm designing a merge helper using BufferGeometryUtils to combine transformed bolt geometries per wheel into a single mesh, keeping the part count manageable.

For glow effects, I'm positioning underglow strips along the chassis edges in cyan, plus magenta accent strips beneath the container edges and corners, giving the vehicle a neon underlighting look before moving on to the front wheel steering joints.

Writing wheel geometry...

Working out that rx = -a solves the rotation correctly, then checking the geometry transform order: rotateX applied before translation when positioning each box.

Now I'm designing the wheel rim with a protruding cylinder for steel paint, a glow ring disc on the outer hub face, and merged nut boxes for the hub detail, while axle rods span across the x-axis at each axle position with a given radius.

For the differential bulge I'm adding a sphere at center, leaf springs as boxes, and a drive shaft cylinder running under the chassis. The cab gets hood scoop, vents, side mirror boxes with glow edges, door seam details, step boards, a winch drum on the bumper, and a roof sensor dome, kept moderately intricate, plus fuel tank cylinders mounted under the chassis sides.

Working out tank cylinder placement so it clears the wheel arches and chassis without visually colliding, adjusting x and z offsets along the way...

I'm also checking the lowest ground clearance point, confirming the tire cylinder radius keeps the rim bottom resting right at zero.

Checking the vertical clearance math confirms the bottom stays within tolerance either way. I'm adjusting the tread block depth so the outer edge doesn't dip too far below the floor, settling on a radius of 0.62 with 0.08 depth. The bumper height at 0.55 looks fine too.

Now I'm working out greeble placement on the container sides—avoiding overlap with the emblem zone by splitting the available space into a lower rivet strip, an upper vent strip, and a rear section, then generating boxes within those safe regions.

Setting up the builder helpers now, defining shorthand functions for creating parts, boxes, and cylinders attached to the chassis bone so I can quickly place geometry at specific offsets.

Textured planes skip the glow treatment since they carry their own material, while the windshield stays unlit too. For the cab extrusion, I'm setting the thickness axis so it cuts symmetrically from the model-space outline, keeping bevels small and corners sharp with no smoothing.

Now I'm adding side armor plates to the cab as angled boxes, then extruding the container shape with a thicker profile and heavier bevel in the armor color. I'm placing a ridge box along the roof deck for added detail, then working out the turret ring and body geometry, positioning the turret joint and sketching the body outline as an extruded profile anchored at its world coordinates.

Repositioning the turret center along z to -1.1, I'm recomputing all the body profile points as offsets from this anchor so the turret sits properly over the container without poking past its front edge. I'm adding a gun mantlet box and the barrel as a cylinder extending forward from the turret.

Now I'm placing the muzzle brakes, heat sleeves, and gun joint for aiming, checking that the barrel length doesn't clip the cab roof. I'm also adding a turret-top sensor sphere with a glow, a camera box, antennas, and angled missile pods on either side built from a housing box plus a grid of six tube launchers.

Still working out the tube arrangement and rotation...

Still positioning missile warheads...

Now adding antenna whips with glowing tips, a satellite dish, and a roof lightbar box positioned above the cab's flat section.

Next I'm working on exhaust stacks—vertical cylinders near the front with heat shield rings and glowing orange caps—plus a roof hatch for the cab, then moving to rear details: glowing red taillight strips and a screen-textured plane on the back door facing outward.

I'm placing hazard bars and a bumper with a hazard texture below the rear door, plus a tow hitch, and refining the chamfered bottom corner where the rear slope meets the back face. Then I'm adding side emblem texture planes positioned just outside the container's bevel edge, sized to fit the side panel, along with vertical rib boxes for extra armored detailing.

Adding stripe details...

For cab decoration, I'm considering a small circle badge texture or a door number graphic, reusing or creating a compact emblem texture to keep the total texture count manageable, then moving to front fender boxes positioned near the wheel wells.

Now I'm working out rear mudguard placement under the container, sizing a thin box spanning both rear wheels and adding small mud flap boxes trailing behind each wheel.

Setting wheel z-positions front and rear, then building the front bumper box with forward-facing ram spike cones and small cyan fog light glows, plus a grille plane on its face.

Writing the HEAD SVG...

Now I'm sketching the WIND panel with a dark gradient background, diagonal reflection polygons, and HUD-style cyan text; the SIDE panel with a magenta-stroked box, hazard block, bold "AEGIS-X" labeling, and barcode details; and starting the RING panel as a circular layout.

For RING, I'm defining concentric circles with a cyan ring, dark core, and spokes radiating outward with a glow effect. SCREEN gets a radar-style display with sweep wedge and blips, HAZ is diagonal warning stripes, and BADGE is a small circular emblem with a star and number.

Writing the wheel geometry loop...

Adding wheel hub details and bolts...

Now I'm positioning the container's roof details -- vents, hatch, pods, turret ring, and dish -- carefully checking their coordinates so they don't overlap on the deck.

Noticing the whip antennas push total height to 4.55, I decide to shorten them to 1.0 units so the overall height stays closer to 3.95. Then I work out mirror arm rods extending from the cab sides outward to small mirror boxes, followed by door seam details using thin dark boxes and handle shapes, plus a step box near the front wheel area.

Still placing truck details...

I'm laying out the chassis frame dimensions and adjusting for the bumper conflict, then adding underbody greeble like crossmembers, diff spheres at the axles, and a driveshaft cylinder. I'm also planning axle cylinders and considering reusing the BADGE texture on cab doors, while tallying up the texture list so far.

Now I'm finalizing paint and metal materials for armor panels, cab, and tires, plus setting accent hex colors, and defining a panelled cab paint variant before writing the dish lathe shape coordinates.

I'm computing the feed arm rod extending from the dish center along the normalized axis direction, setting up mirrored pod arrays for both sides, and assigning materials for the missile pod housing, tubes, and warheads.

Now I'm merging the pod geometries and rotating the combined shape before placing it at the pod position. I'm also adding tail light glow boxes, a red turret eye sphere, a lidar cylinder, and setting up the turret joint with its parent bone connection.

I'm defining the gun joint with its aim target, finishing underglow and canopy details, and double-checking import paths for glow, noise, and panelled metal kits before writing the greeble generation code.

Generating greeble details...
